openings.claim: Test whether requirement-based allocation improves usable access over inherited 90-minute bookings, distinguishing allocation mismatch from room/time scarcity.
openings.discriminator: Compare calendars against identical complete needs; distinguish full satisfaction from minimum access. Persistent unmatched piano/evening requirements indicate constrained scarcity.
openings.fit: Preserves two rooms, existing 24 staffed hours, requested weekly 60-minute entitlements, equipment, both performances, no new fees and telephone/in-person access without accounts. Changes require agreement; shortened, split or outside rehearsals count only if accepted.
openings.probe: Interview all twelve contacts about total weekly needs, acceptable windows, equipment, uninterrupted duration and outstanding needs despite rehearsals elsewhere. Compare inherited and manually reassigned paper calendars. If feasible, confirm assignments through D2 and measure eight weeks of needs met, conflicts and all administration, including collection.
openings.uncertainty: Accurate contact reports and acceptable alternatives are unverified. Aggregate vacancy and late/absent bookings do not prove reclaimable usable time; administration may exceed budget.

openings.claim: One authoritative desk calendar, booking identifiers and confirmed changes may reduce conflicting expectations.
openings.discriminator: Calendar-disagreement conflicts should cease; duplicate arrivals with matching confirmations implicate misunderstanding or another access process.
openings.fit: Preserves telephone/in-person booking and staffed key collection; online copy becomes dated information, with confirmed updates. No account or added staffing.
openings.probe: For two weeks, record volunteer/desk changes before confirming; read back room, date, time and identifier. Log conflicts, stale-copy reliance and amendment effort; retain only if administration supports the target.
openings.uncertainty: Existing coordination may not synchronize reliably; confirmation work may increase administration.
